002-cat-keys.title: A Cat Kept Leaving Him Keys. Then He Found the Door. #shorts
lines: Every morning, the cat left a key on Leo's doormat.
Monday, one key. Tuesday, another. By Friday, he had five.
None of them opened anything. Then he moved the sofa, and found a tiny door in the wall.
The smallest key fit. Click.
Inside: every sock he had ever lost, piled into a bed. The cat strolled in, dropped one more key, and purred: rent.

003-robot-vacuum.title: My Robot Vacuum Avoids One Spot. I Finally Checked. #shorts
lines: My robot vacuum refuses to touch one corner.
Every day it cleans the whole room, stops at the rug, and turns around.
I reset it. I moved the furniture. It still beeps and backs away.
So last night, I lifted the rug.
Under it: Nibbles, my hamster who escaped in March, living in a tiny house made of dust. And my vacuum? It's been bringing him crumbs.

004-3am-pizza.title: He Ordered Pizza at 3 AM. He Delivered It. #shorts
lines: The pizza guy at the door had Theo's face.
Same scar. Same shirt. Same voice.
Large pepperoni, the stranger said. You'll understand soon. Then he walked off into the dark.
The receipt was signed in Theo's own handwriting.
Shaking, he ate a slice and fell asleep on the couch.
He woke up on a doorstep, in a red cap, holding a large pepperoni.
It was three in the morning. He rang the bell.

005-old-photo.title: He Found His Face in a 100-Year-Old Photo. #shorts
lines: Sam found his own face in a hundred-year-old photo.
Same mole. Same watch. The one on his wrist right now.
The seller took one dollar, smiled and said: Took you long enough.
At home, Sam turned the photo over.
On the back, in his own handwriting: Don't buy the watch.
He looked at his wrist. The watch was ticking backwards.
